chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Umairah, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah, who said: Anas narrated to me, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:
Every stubborn tyrant is one who refuses to say 'There is no god but Allah.'

key_terms.جَبَّارٍ: Tyrant; one who is overbearing and domineering
key_terms.عَنِيدٍ: Stubborn; one who is obstinate and refuses to yield
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah; the core declaration of monotheism

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a stubborn tyrant in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith establishes a direct causal link between the theological rejection of *Tawhid* and the emergence of political tyranny, defining the 'stubborn tyrant' not merely by force but by spiritual arrogance. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that true leadership (*Imamah*) is rooted in monotheistic submission, while tyranny arises from the refusal to acknowledge divine sovereignty. The narration underscores that the core of *Jabbariyyah* (tyrannical dominance) is the ego-driven denial of 'La ilaha illa Allah.'
